idee_recherchee.texte: At the centre of a black hole, the equations of general relativity break down into a singularity of infinite density, which shows that our current theories cannot fully describe what happens at extreme gravity.

titre_video: Scientists Are Freaking Out Over Space Time (It's Not Real)
titre: Le mystère de l'intérieur des trous noirs et du paradoxe de l'information
resume: Black holes form from supernovas and collapse into a singularity of infinite gravity, but what happens inside is unknown. Since matter and energy cannot be destroyed, the fallen information must go somewhere, and only a little Hawking radiation escapes, leaving ideas like an alternate dimension or information stuck at the event horizon.
texte: Perhaps the darkest and most mysterious objects in our entire [music] universe are black holes. We know they're everywhere, and scientists have just recently captured the first photograph of these lurking [music] space monsters. Scientists have explained why these phenomena occur, but have no idea what happens inside of [music] a black hole. Black holes are created when a massive star goes supernova, and the star ejects its guts across [music] the galaxy. All that's left is a sphere of densely packed particles that once made up the star's core. The matter in this region of space [music] is so dense, it collapses in on itself, creating a singularity where gravity becomes infinite. The gravity is so strong that nothing can escape its pull, not even light. But the real mystery is what happens inside the black hole. According to the [music] laws of physics, matter and energy cannot be destroyed. This means although a black hole would most certainly crush you [music] with its immense gravity if you ever fell into one, the atoms you're made up of would need to go somewhere. Scientists [music] don't think that all of that information is just stored at the center of the black hole, but since nothing but a small amount of what's called Hawking radiation, named after the famous astronomer Stephen Hawking, leaves a black hole, what happens to all [music] the other things that fall into it is still a mystery. This problem stumps the most brilliant minds that have ever lived, and [music] no solution seems to be in sight. Maybe the singularity at the center of a black hole leads to an alternate dimension where everything that's sucked in ends up. [music] Or perhaps all of this information is just stuck around the event horizon of the black hole. We will most likely never find out in our lifetime, but scientists will never [music] stop trying to uncover the answer to this great mystery of our universe.
